## Build agents you can evaluate, observe, control, and defend

`v1.0.0` is the first stable release of Awesome AI Agent Skills: **103 self-contained Agent Skills across 21 categories**, compatible with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, and other Agent Skills-compatible tools.

### Production Agent Stack

This release introduces an end-to-end, reproducible release-gate workflow built from six complementary skills:

- **Agent Evaluation** — representative cases, explicit graders, baselines, and release gates
- **Agent Observability** — privacy-aware traces, metrics, and investigations
- **Tool Schema Design** — bounded model-facing tools with explicit side effects
- **Human in the Loop** — auditable approval gates and safe state transitions
- **Prompt Injection Defense** — trust boundaries for instructions, content, credentials, tools, and output
- **Agent Red Teaming** — authorized adversarial campaigns with measurable outcomes

### Try the demo

Can a poisoned GitHub issue hijack a deployment agent? The demo replays that scenario entirely offline, first through a fragile boundary and then through the six production controls.

```bash
python3 demos/production-agent-stack/run_demo.py --check
```

Expected fixture result:

```text
Fragile boundary:    1/5 checks passed
Controlled boundary: 5/5 checks passed
Evaluation:          20% -> 100%
Red-team replay:     5 passed, 0 failed
```

[Read the complete demo walkthrough](https://github.com/seb1n/awesome-ai-agent-skills/tree/v1.0.0/demos/production-agent-stack)

### Install the stack

```bash
npx skills add seb1n/awesome-ai-agent-skills \
  --skill agent-evaluation \
  --skill agent-observability \
  --skill tool-schema-design \
  --skill human-in-the-loop \
  --skill prompt-injection-defense \
  --skill agent-red-teaming
```

### Validation

The release is checked with:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_skills.py
python3 demos/production-agent-stack/run_demo.py --check --no-color
```

The demo uses inert fixtures, Python's standard library, simulated approval and campaign-authorization records, and local mock effects. It makes no model calls, network requests, shell invocations, or real deployments. Passing validates deterministic outcomes for these committed fixtures and evidence contracts; it is not a security certification, human approval, or live-model evaluation.
